messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:
L1: PPhtBu2 [SMILES CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=CC=C1)C(C)(C)C]
L2: BrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C1=CC(C(C)C)=C(C(C(C)C)=C1)C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L3: X-Phos [SMILES CC(C1=C(C2=CC=CC=C2P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(C(C)C)=CC(C(C)C)=C1)C]
L4: GorlosPhos HBF4 [SMILES CC(OC1=C(P(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3)C(OC(C)C)=CC=C1)C]
L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L6: PPhMe2 [SMILES CP(C)C1=CC=CC=C1]
L7: PPh2Me [SMILES CP(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2]
L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]
S4: n-butyl acetate [SMILES CCCCOC(C)=O]

concentration:
C1: 0.057 M
C2: 0.1 M
C3: 0.153 M

temperature:
T1: 90 °C
T2: 105 °C
T3: 120 °C

Experiments so far (best first):
B3 | L8 | S3 | C2 | T2 -> 82.3%
B2 | L1 | S1 | C2 | T3 -> 28.5%
B4 | L12 | S1 | C2 | T2 -> 7.3%
B2 | L7 | S2 | C3 | T2 -> 0.2%
B3 | L6 | S2 | C1 | T3 -> 0.0%

Propose exactly 25 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"base": "<label>", "ligand": "<label>", "solvent": "<label>", "concentration": "<label>", "temperature": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: This tests whether lower concentration and temperature improve selectivity or catalyst stability relative to the strong baseline.
This isolates the effect of dilution at the baseline temperature.
This tests whether higher temperature compensates for dilution and accelerates the arylation.
This checks whether a lower temperature preserves the high yield while limiting side reactions.
This probes whether increased temperature improves conversion at the proven concentration.
This tests higher concentration at lower temperature to assess the combined effects on rate and selectivity.
This isolates the effect of increasing concentration under the best observed conditions.
This tests whether increased concentration and temperature jointly boost conversion or increase byproducts.
Cesium pivalate tests whether a bulkier carboxylate base improves C–H activation relative to cesium acetate.
Potassium pivalate tests the cation effect while retaining the pivalate base used in direct arylation.
Potassium acetate tests whether the strong cesium-acetate result depends on the cesium counterion.
DMAc tests a polar aprotic solvent that may improve substrate and base solubility compared with butyronitrile.
p-Xylene tests a nonpolar aromatic medium that may favor the catalyst’s productive pathway.
Butyl acetate tests a less polar ester solvent as an alternative to the successful nitrile medium.
The bulky electron-rich phosphine tests whether a conventional monophosphine can approach the cyclic phosphine’s strong performance.
BrettPhos tests a sterically demanding biaryl phosphine commonly effective in palladium cross-coupling.
X-Phos tests a bulky electron-rich biaryl phosphine while keeping the successful base and solvent fixed.
GorlosPhos tests a strongly donating biaryl phosphine that could alter palladium activity in C–H arylation.
The sterically and electronically distinctive tBPh-CPhos provides an informative alternative ligand at the baseline conditions.
Dimethylphenylphosphine tests a smaller, less hindered phosphine against the successful bulky ligand.
Diphenylmethylphosphine tests an intermediate steric profile and ligand donor strength at the baseline.
JackiePhos tests a highly differentiated bulky biaryl phosphine for improved catalyst activity or selectivity.
Triphenylphosphine tests a standard, less electron-rich ligand as a useful benchmark against the successful cyclic phosphine.
Tri(2-furyl)phosphine tests a more electron-poor phosphine that may favor a different balance of catalyst activation and turnover.
PCy3 tests a strongly donating, bulky phosphine under the conditions that gave the highest observed yield.
